# zppsvx

> Solves a complex Hermitian positive definite system A*X = B where A is in packed storage, with optional equilibration, condition estimation, and error bounds.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import zppsvx from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/zppsvx';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
zppsvx(
    order,
    fact, uplo,
    N, nrhs,
    AP,
    AFP,
    equed,
    S, strideS,
    B, LDB,
    X, LDX,
    rcond,
    FERR, strideFERR,
    BERR, strideBERR,
    WORK,
    RWORK
) → integer
```

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | in |  | one of `'row-major'`, `'column-major'` | storage layout ('row-major' or 'column-major') |
| `fact` | `("not-factored"\|"equilibrate"\|"factored")` | in |  | one of `'equilibrate'`, `'factored'`, `'not-factored'` | 'not-factored', 'factored', or 'equilibrate' |
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | in |  | one of `'lower'`, `'upper'` | 'upper' or 'lower' |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `N ≥ 0` | order of the matrix A |
| `nrhs` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `nrhs ≥ 0` | number of right-hand sides |
| `AP` | `Complex128Array` | in/out | `trunc( N * (N + 1) / 2 )` |  | packed Hermitian positive definite matrix, length N*(N+1)/2 |
| `AFP` | `Complex128Array` | in/out | `trunc( N * (N + 1) / 2 )` |  | factored packed matrix |
| `equed` | `Array.<string>` | in/out |  | rejects `fact === 'factored' && !((equed === 'yes') \|\| equed === 'none')` | single-element array for equilibration status |
| `S` | `Float64Array` | in/out | `N` |  | scaling factors, length N |
| ↳ `strideS` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for S |
| `B` | `Complex128Array` | in/out | `N × nrhs` |  | right-hand side matrix |
| ↳ `LDB` | `PositiveInteger` | in |  | column-major requires `LDB ≥ max( 1, N )`; row-major requires `LDB ≥ max( 1, nrhs )` | leading dimension of B (in complex elements) |
| `X` | `Complex128Array` | out | `N × nrhs` |  | solution matrix (output) |
| ↳ `LDX` | `PositiveInteger` | in |  | column-major requires `LDX ≥ max( 1, N )`; row-major requires `LDX ≥ max( 1, nrhs )` | leading dimension of X (in complex elements) |
| `rcond` | `Float64Array` | out |  |  | single-element array for reciprocal condition number |
| `FERR` | `Float64Array` | out | `nrhs` |  | forward error bounds (output) |
| ↳ `strideFERR` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for FERR |
| `BERR` | `Float64Array` | out | `nrhs` |  | backward error bounds (output) |
| ↳ `strideBERR` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for BERR |
| `WORK` | `(Complex128Array\|null)` | out | `≥ 2 * N` |  | complex workspace array |
| `RWORK` | `(Float64Array\|null)` | out | `≥ N` |  | real workspace array |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `fact`: Specifies whether or not the factored form of the matrix A is supplied on entry, and if not, whether the matrix A should be equilibrated before it is factored.

  -   `= 'F'`: On entry, `AFP` contains the factored form of A. If `EQUED = 'Y'`, the matrix A has been equilibrated with scaling factors given by S.  `AP` and `AFP` will not be modified.
  -   `= 'N'`: The matrix A will be copied to `AFP` and factored.
  -   `= 'E'`: The matrix A will be equilibrated if necessary, then copied to `AFP` and factored.
- `uplo`:

  -   `= 'U'`: Upper triangle of A is stored;
  -   `= 'L'`: Lower triangle of A is stored.
- `N`: The number of linear equations, i.e., the order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `nrhs`: The number of right hand sides, i.e., the number of columns of the matrices B and X. $\mathrm{NRHS} \ge 0$.
- `AP`: On entry, the upper or lower triangle of the Hermitian matrix A, packed columnwise in a linear array, except if `FACT = 'F'` and `EQUED = 'Y'`, then A must contain the equilibrated matrix $\operatorname{diag}(S) \, A \, \operatorname{diag}(S)$. The j-th column of A is stored in the array `AP` as follows: if `UPLO = 'U'`, `AP(i + (j-1)*j/2) = A(i,j)` for $1 \le i \le j$; if `UPLO = 'L'`, `AP(i + (j-1)*(2n-j)/2) = A(i,j)` for $j \le i \le n$. See below for further details. A is not modified if `FACT = 'F'` or 'N', or if `FACT = 'E'` and `EQUED = 'N'` on exit.

  On exit, if `FACT = 'E'` and `EQUED = 'Y'`, A is overwritten by $\operatorname{diag}(S) \, A \, \operatorname{diag}(S)$.
- `AFP`: If `FACT = 'F'`, then `AFP` is an input argument and on entry contains the triangular factor U or L from the Cholesky factorization $A = U^H \, U$ or $A = L \, L^H$, in the same storage format as A. If $\mathrm{EQUED} \ne \text{'N'}$, then `AFP` is the factored form of the equilibrated matrix A.

  If `FACT = 'N'`, then `AFP` is an output argument and on exit returns the triangular factor U or L from the Cholesky factorization $A = U^H \, U$ or $A = L \, L^H$ of the original matrix A.

  If `FACT = 'E'`, then `AFP` is an output argument and on exit returns the triangular factor U or L from the Cholesky factorization $A = U^H \, U$ or $A = L \, L^H$ of the equilibrated matrix A (see the description of `AP` for the form of the equilibrated matrix).
- `equed`: Specifies the form of equilibration that was done.

  -   `= 'N'`: No equilibration (always true if `FACT = 'N'`).
  -   `= 'Y'`: Equilibration was done, i.e., A has been replaced by $\operatorname{diag}(S) \, A \, \operatorname{diag}(S)$. `EQUED` is an input argument if `FACT = 'F'`; otherwise, it is an output argument.
- `S`: The scale factors for A; not accessed if `EQUED = 'N'`. S is an input argument if `FACT = 'F'`; otherwise, S is an output argument. If `FACT = 'F'` and `EQUED = 'Y'`, each element of S must be positive.
- `B`: On entry, the N-by-`NRHS` right hand side matrix B. On exit, if `EQUED = 'N'`, B is not modified; if `EQUED = 'Y'`, B is overwritten by $\operatorname{diag}(S) \, B$.
- `X`: If `INFO = 0` or $\mathrm{INFO} = N+1$, the N-by-`NRHS` solution matrix X to the original system of equations. Note that if `EQUED = 'Y'`, A and B are modified on exit, and the solution to the equilibrated system is $\operatorname{inv}(\operatorname{diag}(S)) \, X$.
- `rcond`: The estimate of the reciprocal condition number of the matrix A after equilibration (if done). If `RCOND` is less than the machine precision (in particular, if `RCOND = 0`), the matrix is singular to working precision. This condition is indicated by a return code of $\mathrm{INFO} > 0$.
- `FERR`: The estimated forward error bound for each solution vector `X(j)` (the j-th column of the solution matrix X). If XTRUE is the true solution corresponding to `X(j)`, `FERR(j)` is an estimated upper bound for the magnitude of the largest element in (`X(j)` - XTRUE) divided by the magnitude of the largest element in `X(j)`. The estimate is as reliable as the estimate for `RCOND`, and is almost always a slight overestimate of the true error.
- `BERR`: The componentwise relative backward error of each solution vector `X(j)` (i.e., the smallest relative change in any element of A or B that makes `X(j)` an exact solution).

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: info

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `TypeError` second argument must be one of the following: "equilibrate", "factored", "not-factored"
- `TypeError` third argument must be a valid matrix triangle
- `RangeError` fourth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` fifth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `TypeError` eighth argument is invalid (rejected when `fact === "factored" && !( ( equed[ 0 ] === "yes" ) \|\| equed[ 0 ] === "none" )`)
- `RangeError` twelfth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )` (column-major)
- `RangeError` twelfth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, nrhs )` (row-major)
- `RangeError` fourteenth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )` (column-major)
- `RangeError` fourteenth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, nrhs )` (row-major)
- `TypeError` if a string argument is not a valid option

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
zppsvx.ndarray(
    fact, uplo,
    N, nrhs,
    AP, strideAP, offsetAP,
    AFP, strideAFP, offsetAFP,
    equed,
    S, strideS, offsetS,
    B, strideB1, strideB2, offsetB,
    X, strideX1, strideX2, offsetX,
    rcond,
    FERR, strideFERR, offsetFERR,
    BERR, strideBERR, offsetBERR,
    WORK, strideWork, offsetWork,
    RWORK, strideRWork, offsetRWork
) → info: integer
```

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `fact` | `("not-factored"\|"equilibrate"\|"factored")` | in |  | one of `'equilibrate'`, `'factored'`, `'not-factored'` | `'not-factored'`, `'factored'`, or `'equilibrate'` |
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | in |  | one of `'lower'`, `'upper'` | `'upper'` or `'lower'` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `N ≥ 0` | order of the matrix A |
| `nrhs` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `nrhs ≥ 0` | number of right-hand side columns |
| `AP` | `Complex128Array` | in/out | `trunc( N * (N + 1) / 2 )` |  | Hermitian positive definite matrix in packed storage (length N*(N+1)/2) |
| ↳ `strideAP` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for AP (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetAP` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for AP (in complex elements) |
| `AFP` | `Complex128Array` | in/out | `trunc( N * (N + 1) / 2 )` |  | factored form in packed storage |
| ↳ `strideAFP` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for AFP (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetAFP` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for AFP (in complex elements) |
| `equed` | `Array.<string>` | in/out |  | rejects `fact === 'factored' && !((equed === 'yes') \|\| equed === 'none')` | single-element array for equilibration status ('none' or 'yes') |
| `S` | `Float64Array` | in/out | `N` |  | scaling factors (length N) |
| ↳ `strideS` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for S |
| ↳ `offsetS` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for S |
| `B` | `Complex128Array` | in/out | `N × nrhs` |  | right-hand side matrix (column-major, N-by-NRHS, in complex elements) |
| ↳ `strideB1` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the first dimension of B (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `strideB2` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the second dimension of B (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetB` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for B (in complex elements) |
| `X` | `Complex128Array` | out | `N × nrhs` |  | solution matrix (column-major, N-by-NRHS, output, in complex elements) |
| ↳ `strideX1` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the first dimension of X (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `strideX2` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the second dimension of X (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetX` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for X (in complex elements) |
| `rcond` | `Float64Array` | out |  |  | single-element array for reciprocal condition number (output) |
| `FERR` | `Float64Array` | out | `nrhs` |  | forward error bounds array (length NRHS, output) |
| ↳ `strideFERR` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for FERR |
| ↳ `offsetFERR` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for FERR |
| `BERR` | `Float64Array` | out | `nrhs` |  | backward error bounds array (length NRHS, output) |
| ↳ `strideBERR` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for BERR |
| ↳ `offsetBERR` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for BERR |
| `WORK` | `Complex128Array` | out | `≥ 2 * N` |  | complex workspace array (length at least 2*N) |
| ↳ `strideWork` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for WORK (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for WORK (in complex elements) |
| `RWORK` | `Float64Array` | out | `≥ N` |  | real workspace array (length at least N) |
| ↳ `strideRWork` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for RWORK |
| ↳ `offsetRWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for RWORK |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `fact`: Specifies whether or not the factored form of the matrix A is supplied on entry, and if not, whether the matrix A should be equilibrated before it is factored.

  -   `= 'F'`: On entry, `AFP` contains the factored form of A. If `EQUED = 'Y'`, the matrix A has been equilibrated with scaling factors given by S.  `AP` and `AFP` will not be modified.
  -   `= 'N'`: The matrix A will be copied to `AFP` and factored.
  -   `= 'E'`: The matrix A will be equilibrated if necessary, then copied to `AFP` and factored.
- `uplo`:

  -   `= 'U'`: Upper triangle of A is stored;
  -   `= 'L'`: Lower triangle of A is stored.
- `N`: The number of linear equations, i.e., the order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `nrhs`: The number of right hand sides, i.e., the number of columns of the matrices B and X. $\mathrm{NRHS} \ge 0$.
- `AP`: On entry, the upper or lower triangle of the Hermitian matrix A, packed columnwise in a linear array, except if `FACT = 'F'` and `EQUED = 'Y'`, then A must contain the equilibrated matrix $\operatorname{diag}(S) \, A \, \operatorname{diag}(S)$. The j-th column of A is stored in the array `AP` as follows: if `UPLO = 'U'`, `AP(i + (j-1)*j/2) = A(i,j)` for $1 \le i \le j$; if `UPLO = 'L'`, `AP(i + (j-1)*(2n-j)/2) = A(i,j)` for $j \le i \le n$. See below for further details. A is not modified if `FACT = 'F'` or 'N', or if `FACT = 'E'` and `EQUED = 'N'` on exit.

  On exit, if `FACT = 'E'` and `EQUED = 'Y'`, A is overwritten by $\operatorname{diag}(S) \, A \, \operatorname{diag}(S)$.
- `AFP`: If `FACT = 'F'`, then `AFP` is an input argument and on entry contains the triangular factor U or L from the Cholesky factorization $A = U^H \, U$ or $A = L \, L^H$, in the same storage format as A. If $\mathrm{EQUED} \ne \text{'N'}$, then `AFP` is the factored form of the equilibrated matrix A.

  If `FACT = 'N'`, then `AFP` is an output argument and on exit returns the triangular factor U or L from the Cholesky factorization $A = U^H \, U$ or $A = L \, L^H$ of the original matrix A.

  If `FACT = 'E'`, then `AFP` is an output argument and on exit returns the triangular factor U or L from the Cholesky factorization $A = U^H \, U$ or $A = L \, L^H$ of the equilibrated matrix A (see the description of `AP` for the form of the equilibrated matrix).
- `equed`: Specifies the form of equilibration that was done.

  -   `= 'N'`: No equilibration (always true if `FACT = 'N'`).
  -   `= 'Y'`: Equilibration was done, i.e., A has been replaced by $\operatorname{diag}(S) \, A \, \operatorname{diag}(S)$. `EQUED` is an input argument if `FACT = 'F'`; otherwise, it is an output argument.
- `S`: The scale factors for A; not accessed if `EQUED = 'N'`. S is an input argument if `FACT = 'F'`; otherwise, S is an output argument. If `FACT = 'F'` and `EQUED = 'Y'`, each element of S must be positive.
- `B`: On entry, the N-by-`NRHS` right hand side matrix B. On exit, if `EQUED = 'N'`, B is not modified; if `EQUED = 'Y'`, B is overwritten by $\operatorname{diag}(S) \, B$.
- `X`: If `INFO = 0` or $\mathrm{INFO} = N+1$, the N-by-`NRHS` solution matrix X to the original system of equations. Note that if `EQUED = 'Y'`, A and B are modified on exit, and the solution to the equilibrated system is $\operatorname{inv}(\operatorname{diag}(S)) \, X$.
- `rcond`: The estimate of the reciprocal condition number of the matrix A after equilibration (if done). If `RCOND` is less than the machine precision (in particular, if `RCOND = 0`), the matrix is singular to working precision. This condition is indicated by a return code of $\mathrm{INFO} > 0$.
- `FERR`: The estimated forward error bound for each solution vector `X(j)` (the j-th column of the solution matrix X). If XTRUE is the true solution corresponding to `X(j)`, `FERR(j)` is an estimated upper bound for the magnitude of the largest element in (`X(j)` - XTRUE) divided by the magnitude of the largest element in `X(j)`. The estimate is as reliable as the estimate for `RCOND`, and is almost always a slight overestimate of the true error.
- `BERR`: The componentwise relative backward error of each solution vector `X(j)` (i.e., the smallest relative change in any element of A or B that makes `X(j)` an exact solution).

</details>

**Returns** `info: integer`: 0 if successful, k>0 if factorization failed, N+1 if rcond < machine epsilon

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be one of the following: "equilibrate", "factored", "not-factored"
- `TypeError` second argument must be a valid matrix triangle
- `RangeError` third argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` fourth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `TypeError` eleventh argument is invalid (rejected when `fact === "factored" && !( ( equed[ 0 ] === "yes" ) \|\| equed[ 0 ] === "none" )`)
- `RangeError` `RWORK` must have at least `N` elements from `offsetRWork`

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value
-   `> 0`: if `INFO = i`, and i is \<= N:  the leading principal minor of order i of A is not positive, so the factorization could not be completed, and the solution has not been computed. `RCOND = 0` is returned. = N+1: U is nonsingular, but `RCOND` is less than machine precision, meaning that the matrix is singular to working precision.  Nevertheless, the solution and error bounds are computed because there are a number of situations where the computed solution can be more accurate than the value of `RCOND` would suggest.

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Complex128Array from '@stdlib/array/complex128/lib/index.js';
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import reinterpret from '@stdlib/strided/base/reinterpret-complex128/lib/index.js';
import zppsvx from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/zppsvx';

// 3x3 Hermitian positive definite matrix in upper packed storage.

// A = [10  3-i  1+2i;  3+i  8  2-i;  1-2i  2+i  6]
const AP = new Complex128Array( new Float64Array( [ 10, 0, 3, -1, 8, 0, 1, 2, 2, -1, 6, 0 ] ) ); // eslint-disable-line max-len
const AFP = new Complex128Array( 6 );
const S = new Float64Array( 3 );
const equed = [ 'none' ];
const B = new Complex128Array( new Float64Array( [ 1, 1, 2, -1, 3, 0.5 ] ) );
const X = new Complex128Array( 3 );
const rcond = new Float64Array( 1 );
const FERR = new Float64Array( 1 );
const BERR = new Float64Array( 1 );
const WORK = new Complex128Array( 6 );
const RWORK = new Float64Array( 3 );

const info = zppsvx.ndarray( 'not-factored', 'upper', 3, 1, AP, 1, 0, AFP, 1, 0, equed, S, 1, 0, B, 1, 3, 0, X, 1, 3, 0, rcond, FERR, 1, 0, BERR, 1, 0, WORK, 1, 0, RWORK, 1, 0 ); // eslint-disable-line max-len

console.log( 'info:', info ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( 'X:', reinterpret( X, 0 ) ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( 'rcond:', rcond[ 0 ] ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( 'FERR:', FERR[ 0 ] ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( 'BERR:', BERR[ 0 ] ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `ZPPSVX`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

ZPPSVX uses the Cholesky factorization $A = U^H \, U$ or $A = L \, L^H$ to compute the solution to a complex system of linear equations

$$
A \, X = B
$$

where A is an N-by-N Hermitian positive definite matrix stored in packed format and X and B are N-by-`NRHS` matrices.

Error bounds on the solution and a condition estimate are also provided.

### Further Details

The packed storage scheme is illustrated by the following example when $N = 4$, `UPLO = 'U'`:

Two-dimensional storage of the Hermitian matrix A:

a11 a12 a13 a14

a22 a23 a24 a33 a34 (aij = conjg(aji)) a44

Packed storage of the upper triangle of A:

`AP` = \[ a11, a12, a22, a13, a23, a33, a14, a24, a34, a44 \]

</section>
